domain_label: Plated-Jewelry Assortment — Demand-Signal Synthesis & Ranked Candidate List
purpose: A method for fusing three demand signals of different reliability — the S1 US-market read from public data, the S4 paid IG/TikTok poll, and the owner's own existing on-site/bestseller history ('mindful of the old stuff') — into one reliability-weighted, uncertainty-tagged, ABC/Pareto-classified ranked candidate list of plated-jewelry SKUs, so a coherent launch six can be selected downstream, without over-fitting to thin store history or fabricating any demand number the signals have not actually measured.
assumptions: no demand dataset is supplied inside this KB; every score here is a heuristic prior about the METHOD, not a measured sell-through, and the actual signal values are produced later by the S1 public-data pull and the S4 poll

three signal sources feed this KB and only three: S1 market read (public marketplace best-seller ranks, search volume, retail-assortment share), S4 paid social poll (category/shape preference), and the owner's existing storefront analytics (views, add-to-cart, orders, bestseller history) — each carrying different reliability, lag and bias

the candidate unit is a SKU-candidate defined on the shared dimensions category x form/shape x finish-tier x price-band inherited from S1/S3, so all three signals can be mapped onto one common candidate frame

ABC/Pareto (the ~80/20 concentration heuristic) and the long-tail structure are real, well-established assortment/inventory concepts [FACT] and are used as classification lenses, never as invented share percentages for this specific catalog

existing store history is treated as a biased, survivorship- and availability-limited sample (you only have data on what you already stocked and showed), so it informs but never dictates the ranking; regression-to-the-mean and shrinkage-to-prior are applied [FACT-method]

every non-fact is tagged [ESTIMATE] (with method + confidence), [METHOD] (a way to obtain the number) or [UNKNOWN]; no market size, unit-sales count, gold-plated-vs-solid percentage, ethnicity purchase rate, competitor brand or price is asserted as measured anywhere in this KB
exclusions: generating the raw signals themselves — the S1 public-data demand read, the S4 poll instrument and its fielding, and the S3 shape/style taxonomy are owned by those specialists; this KB consumes their outputs

constructing the final coherent launch set of six (category coverage, price-spread, cohesion, MOQ/plating-run/capital pruning) — that is kb2_launch_set_of_six; this KB stops at a ranked, classified candidate list
the post-launch test-measure-cut/keep/expand loop and refresh cadence — that is kb3_test_iterate_protocol
unit economics, COGS, pricing and viability (the jewel_economics specialist); ranking here is by demand signal, not by margin, though price-band is carried as a candidate dimension
asserting any concrete demand figure, market share, buyer count or competitor fact as measured; this KB encodes only the synthesis-and-ranking method and its honest uncertainty

competency_questions.question: What is the unit being ranked, and on what shared dimensions are the three signals made commensurable?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CANDIDATE_UNIVERSE_FRAME defines a SKU-candidate on category x form/shape x finish-tier x price-band and states that all three signals must be mapped onto this frame before any synthesis

competency_questions.question: Which demand signals feed the synthesis, what is each one's provenance, and how is the owner's existing store data ingested?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_INVENTORY enumerates the S1 market read, the S4 poll and the owner's storefront history with each one's provenance and lag, and EXISTING_STORE_DATA_INTAKE states how the on-site/bestseller history is pulled, normalized and de-staled

competency_questions.question: How is each signal's reliability graded so that more trustworthy signals count for more?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_RELIABILITY_GRADING scores each source on sample size, representativeness, self-selection/survivorship bias, recency and directness-to-purchase, producing a per-signal reliability weight input

competency_questions.question: How is the owner's existing store data used 'mindful of the old stuff' without over-fitting the launch to a small, stale, survivorship-biased history?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXISTING_STORE_DATA_INTAKE, RECENCY_DECAY_WEIGHTING and OVERFIT_GUARD_EXISTING_DATA together apply time-decay to old records, shrink thin per-SKU history toward the market prior, and forbid ranking a candidate on store history alone

competency_questions.question: How are signals measured in different units (marketplace ranks, poll vote shares, on-site conversion) made comparable before they are combined?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NORMALIZATION_COMMENSURATION converts each signal to a common comparable scale (rank-normalization or z-score / min-max) per candidate, so no single high-variance signal dominates by unit artifact

competency_questions.question: How are signals of different reliability weighted and combined into one composite demand score per candidate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WEIGHTING_SCHEME sets reliability-proportional weights and SIGNAL_COMBINATION_RULE combines the normalized signals (reliability-weighted mean or rank aggregation with Bayesian shrinkage) into one composite score that recomputes from the stated inputs

competency_questions.question: What happens when the signals disagree — the poll loves a shape the bestseller history never sold, or the market read contradicts the store data?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIGNAL_CONFLICT_RESOLUTION states the tie-break (reliability-weight order, agreement bonus, disagreement penalty) and NOVELTY_VS_PROVEN_COLDSTART handles the cold-start candidate with no store history so novelty is not auto-penalized to zero

competency_questions.question: How is uncertainty attached to each candidate's score, and when is the combined signal too thin to rank a candidate at all?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_PER_CANDIDATE attaches an interval/confidence to each composite score and MINIMUM_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD defines the floor of signal below which a candidate is parked as [UNKNOWN] not ranked on noise

competency_questions.question: How is the ranked candidate list produced, and why is it ranked within strata rather than one global list?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RANKED_CANDIDATE_LIST outputs the ordered candidate list with composite score + confidence, and TIER_STRATIFIED_RANKING ranks within category and price-band strata so one popular category does not crowd the whole list

competency_questions.question: How is the ranked list classified by demand concentration using ABC/Pareto, and how concentrated is the demand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ABC_PARETO_CLASSIFICATION sorts candidates into A/B/C bands by cumulative signal share against the ~80/20 heuristic [FACT], and DEMAND_CONCENTRATION_DIAGNOSTIC measures how top-heavy the curve is (concentration ratio / Gini-style read) to size the A band

competency_questions.question: How does the classification translate into a hero-SKU vs long-tail structure for the launch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HERO_VS_LONGTAIL maps the A band to hero-SKU candidates and the B/C tail to optional long-tail/coverage picks, stating the tradeoff between concentrating bets on heroes and spreading for coverage

competency_questions.question: How robust is the ranking to the weight choices, how is honesty enforced, and what is handed to the launch-set builder?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENSITIVITY_ROBUSTNESS_CHECK re-runs the ranking under weight perturbation to flag order-flips, HONESTY_LEDGER tags every figure [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN], and RANKED_LIST_HANDOFF delivers the ranked, ABC-classified, hero/tail-labelled list with its confidence and out-of-scope boundary to kb2

glossary.definition: The unit being ranked here: a candidate item defined on the shared dimensions category x form/shape x finish-tier x price-band (e.g. 'small rhodium-plated-silver hoop, mid-tier') onto which each of the three demand signals is mapped so they can be combined; it is a candidate to be launched, not yet a stocked SKU.

A per-source multiplier reflecting how trustworthy a signal is, scored on sample size, representativeness of the target 18-25 female US buyer, self-selection / survivorship / availability bias, recency/lag, and directness-to-purchase; a marketplace best-seller rank (revealed purchase) generally outranks a free-incentive poll vote (stated, self-selected preference), which outranks thin stale store history [METHOD, not a fixed number].

The error of ranking the launch on the owner's existing on-site/bestseller data as if it were representative future demand, when it is a small, stale, survivorship-biased sample of only what was already stocked and shown; guarded by recency decay, shrinkage toward the market prior, and a rule that store data alone never ranks a candidate [FACT-method: regression to the mean, regularization].

Converting signals expressed in different units (marketplace rank, poll vote share, on-site conversion rate) into one comparable scale per candidate — rank-normalization, z-score or min-max — so a signal with a large native range does not dominate the composite by unit artifact rather than by importance [FACT-method].

Combining the normalized signals into one composite demand score as a weighted aggregate (weighted mean of normalized scores, or Borda-style rank aggregation) with weights proportional to signal reliability, plus Bayesian shrinkage that pulls thin-evidence candidates toward the prior [FACT-method]; the whole output of the core of this KB.

The inventory-assortment lens that sorts ranked candidates by cumulative demand-signal share into A (the vital few driving most signal, ~top ~20% carrying ~80%), B (moderate) and C (the long tail); the ~80/20 split is the Pareto heuristic [FACT], used here as a shape to read the curve, never as an invented share number for this catalog.

The A-band, high-signal candidates that justify concentrated inventory and marketing bets (heroes) versus the B/C-band candidates that add coverage, cross-sell and stacking breadth but individually carry little signal (long tail) [FACT-concept, long-tail: Anderson]; the launch must decide how much to concentrate vs spread.

A candidate with no existing store history (a new shape/finish the owner has never stocked) whose store-data signal is absent, not zero; ranked from the S1 market + S4 poll signals and shrunk toward the category prior so a genuinely promising novel item is not auto-buried by a missing history [FACT-method: cold-start problem in recommender systems].

The floor of combined, reliability-weighted evidence below which a candidate's rank would be driven by noise; below it the candidate is parked as [UNKNOWN] / needs-more-signal (feed it into the next S4 poll wave) rather than ranked on a spurious position.

Re-running the composite ranking under perturbed signal weights (e.g. down-weighting the poll, up-weighting revealed purchase) to see which candidate orderings flip; a robust top set that survives reasonable weight changes is trustworthy, while an order that flips on a small weight nudge is flagged as weight-artifact, not real signal.

nodes.definition: Define the unit that gets ranked and the shared coordinate frame that makes three heterogeneous signals combinable: a SKU-candidate = category (earring/necklace/ring/bracelet/anklet) x form/shape (stud/hoop/drop; chain/pendant; band; etc. from S3) x finish-tier (gold-plated / vermeil / gold-filled / rhodium-plated-silver / stainless, per the FTC-anchored S1/S2 definitions [FACT-16 CFR 23]) x price-band. Every signal (market read, poll, store history) must be mapped onto this frame before synthesis; a signal at a coarser grain (e.g. a poll that only says 'earrings') is carried at that grain and spread across its children with an explicit [ESTIMATE] flag, never silently sharpened to a specific SKU.

included: the SKU-candidate definition on category x shape x finish-tier x price-band
the rule that every signal maps onto this frame at its true grain
coarse-grain signals carried as [ESTIMATE] spread, not sharpened
excluded: generating the taxonomy itself (S1/S3 own it)

pros.claim: A shared candidate frame is what lets three unlike signals be combined at all instead of compared apples-to-oranges
pros.example: mapping a marketplace best-seller rank, a poll 'earrings' vote and an on-site hoop conversion all onto the same hoop candidate row makes their synthesis meaningful

cons.claim: Too fine a frame explodes the candidate count and starves each cell of signal; too coarse a frame hides real winners
cons.example: splitting hoops into 12 diameters when the poll only resolves 'hoops' spreads one vote across 12 empty cells

failure_modes: sharpening a coarse 'earrings' poll signal into a specific stud SKU it never measured
defining the frame so finely that every candidate cell is signal-starved
acceptance_tests: the SKU-candidate is defined on category x shape x finish-tier x price-band and the rule that coarse signals are carried at their true grain (flagged [ESTIMATE]) not sharpened is stated
revisit_triggers: S3 revises the shape/style taxonomy
the poll resolves a finer grain than the frame assumed
the candidate count is too sparse or too dense per cell

base.update_signal: the taxonomy grain or the candidate-cell density changes

nodes.definition: Enumerate the exactly-three demand signals and pin each one's provenance, unit, lag and inherent bias so nothing is combined blind: (1) S1 market read — public marketplace best-seller ranks, search-volume trends, retail-assortment share; revealed-ish, broad-market, lags real time by platform-index cadence, biased toward large incumbents [METHOD-source]; (2) S4 paid IG/TikTok poll — stated category/shape preference from the ~18-25 female target, fast and targetable but self-selected and incentive-skewed [METHOD-source]; (3) owner storefront history — on-site views, add-to-cart, orders, bestseller list; the most owner-specific and revealed but the smallest, stalest and survivorship-limited sample. No fourth signal is invented, and no signal's actual values are asserted here — only its identity, unit and bias.

included: the three signal sources with provenance, unit, lag and bias
the no-fourth-signal discipline
identity/unit only, never asserted values

pros.claim: Naming each signal's provenance and bias up front prevents a fast-but-biased poll being treated as ground truth
pros.example: labelling the poll 'stated, self-selected, incentive-skewed' stops a giveaway-inflated 'earrings' vote from being read as revealed demand

cons.claim: Restricting to three sources can miss a signal (e.g. returns data, wishlist) that a mature store would have
cons.example: an owner with rich email/wishlist data has a fourth revealed signal this frame would omit until added

failure_modes: treating the poll's stated preference as revealed purchase
silently importing a signal without recording its lag and bias
acceptance_tests: the S1 market read, S4 poll and owner storefront history are each stated with provenance, unit, lag and bias, and no signal value is asserted as measured
revisit_triggers: a new signal source (returns, wishlist, email) becomes available
a platform changes how its best-seller rank or poll data is exposed
the poll's incentive design changes its bias profile

base.update_signal: a signal source is added, removed or its exposure changes

nodes.definition: Specify how the owner's existing on-site/bestseller data is ingested 'mindful of the old stuff': pull views, add-to-cart, orders and the bestseller list per existing SKU; map each onto the candidate frame; and explicitly characterize the sample's limits — it covers only what was already stocked and merchandised (availability/survivorship bias: a shape never carried shows zero not because buyers rejected it but because it was never offered), it is small (a young store's order counts are thin), and it is stale (old seasons/prices). Convert raw counts to rates (conversion, attach) to reduce traffic-volume artifacts, and hand the de-biased, frame-mapped store signal forward tagged [ESTIMATE, method+confidence] — never as a projected demand truth.

included: pulling and frame-mapping on-site/bestseller data
naming survivorship/availability, small-sample and staleness limits
converting counts to rates and tagging [ESTIMATE]

pros.claim: Characterizing the store sample's survivorship and staleness up front stops the owner's history from being read as unbiased future demand
pros.example: flagging that an anklet's zero sales reflect it never being stocked, not rejection, keeps a viable candidate alive

cons.claim: Rate conversion and de-biasing cannot manufacture signal that a tiny order history simply does not contain
cons.example: three lifetime orders of a ring yield a conversion rate too noisy to trust however it is cleaned

failure_modes: reading a never-stocked shape's zero as demand rejection
using raw order counts so high-traffic pages look like winners by volume alone
acceptance_tests: the store-data pull is stated with frame-mapping, the survivorship/availability + small-sample + staleness limits, count-to-rate conversion, and an [ESTIMATE] tag on the output
revisit_triggers: the store accumulates materially more orders
a previously never-stocked category is trialled, filling a data gap
the analytics source or attribution window changes

base.update_signal: the store data volume, recency or attribution changes

nodes.definition: Grade each of the three signals on five axes to produce a per-signal reliability weight input: sample size, representativeness of the target US 18-25 female buyer, bias load (self-selection + incentive skew for the poll; survivorship/availability for store data; incumbent skew for market ranks), recency/lag, and directness-to-purchase (revealed purchase > stated preference > engagement proxy). The grading is a METHOD producing an ordinal-to-cardinal reliability score per signal, typically ranking revealed marketplace/store purchase above a free-incentive poll vote, and above a thin stale history — but the exact scores are re-derived from the actual signals, never fixed here as invented constants.

included: the five reliability axes
revealed > stated > proxy ordering
reliability as re-derived score not fixed constant
excluded: converting the grade into a combination weight (WEIGHTING_SCHEME)

pros.claim: A five-axis grade turns vague 'trust the poll less' intuition into an auditable per-signal weight input
pros.example: scoring the incentive poll low on bias-load and directness justifies giving it less say than revealed store purchases

cons.claim: Reliability grading is itself judgemental, so a mis-scored axis silently mis-weights everything downstream
cons.example: over-rating the poll's representativeness because it targeted 18-25 while ignoring its self-selection inflates its weight

failure_modes: scoring only sample size and ignoring bias load
hard-coding a reliability constant instead of re-deriving it from the actual fielded signal
acceptance_tests: each signal is graded on sample size, representativeness, bias load, recency and directness-to-purchase, with the revealed>stated>proxy ordering stated and the score noted as re-derived not fixed
revisit_triggers: a signal's sample size or bias profile changes
the poll's targeting or incentive changes its representativeness
a validation of one signal against realized sales lands

base.update_signal: a signal's sample, bias or representativeness changes

nodes.definition: Operationalize 'mindful of the old stuff' as an explicit recency decay on the store history: weight each historical record by a decay function of its age (e.g. exponential half-life on order recency) so last-quarter behaviour counts more than two-year-old behaviour, because fashion-jewelry preference and the store's own audience drift. Decay is applied before the store signal enters the composite, and the chosen half-life is a tunable [ESTIMATE] tied to the category's trend velocity — fast-moving Y2K/coastal fads decay faster than evergreen studs/hoops. Decay reduces stale-data weight without discarding it, keeping small histories usable but appropriately discounted.

included: age-decay weighting of store records
half-life tied to category trend velocity as [ESTIMATE]
decay before entering the composite

pros.claim: Explicit decay stops a two-year-old bestseller from being ranked as if it were current demand
pros.example: an old rhinestone piece that peaked in a past trend decays out of the A band instead of anchoring the launch

cons.claim: An over-aggressive half-life can erase a genuinely evergreen winner's long track record
cons.example: decaying a perennial plain-hoop bestseller too fast throws away its most reliable evidence

failure_modes: applying one half-life to fast-fad and evergreen categories alike
decaying so hard that thin recent data becomes pure noise
acceptance_tests: a recency-decay weighting on store records is stated with an age-decay function and a category-trend-velocity-tied half-life tagged [ESTIMATE], applied before the composite
revisit_triggers: a category's trend velocity shifts (fad emerges or fades)
the store's audience composition changes
a decayed record is validated against a fresh reorder

base.update_signal: category trend velocity or store audience shifts

nodes.definition: Put the three signals on one comparable scale per candidate before any weighting, because they live in different units — marketplace best-seller rank (ordinal, inverted), poll vote share (proportion), on-site conversion/attach rate (proportion with different base). Convert each to a common scale via rank-normalization (map to percentile within its own signal) or standardization (z-score / min-max), so a signal with a wide native range cannot dominate the composite by unit artifact. Rank-normalization is the robust default when a signal is ordinal or heavy-tailed; z-score suits roughly symmetric rate signals. The transform is stated per signal so the composite is reproducible.

included: per-signal transform to a common scale
rank-normalization vs z-score/min-max choice
stated transform for reproducibility

pros.claim: Common-scale normalization stops a wide-range signal from dominating purely by its units
pros.example: converting a 1-10000 marketplace rank and a 0-1 poll share to percentiles lets them contribute comparably

cons.claim: Normalization can compress meaningful magnitude gaps (a runaway top seller looks one rank ahead)
cons.example: rank-normalizing flattens a candidate that outsells the field 10x into merely 'rank 1'

failure_modes: combining raw un-normalized signals so the widest-unit signal silently wins
z-scoring a heavy-tailed ordinal signal where rank-normalization was appropriate
acceptance_tests: each signal's transform to a common comparable scale (rank-normalization or z-score/min-max) is stated per signal so the composite reproduces
revisit_triggers: a signal's distribution shape changes materially
a magnitude gap is being lost that matters to the decision
a new signal with a different unit is added

base.update_signal: a signal distribution or unit changes

nodes.definition: Set the combination weights on the normalized signals proportional to their reliability grades: the more trustworthy signal (typically revealed marketplace/store purchase) carries more weight than the stated, incentive-skewed poll, which carries more than a thin stale history — but no weight is zero unless a signal is absent for that candidate. The scheme is a METHOD: weights are derived from SIGNAL_RELIABILITY_GRADING, stated explicitly (e.g. a documented split rather than a hidden default), and held as a small set of scenarios (revealed-heavy, balanced, poll-informed) so the ranking's dependence on the weight choice can be tested downstream. Weights are re-derived per fielding, never asserted as universal constants.

included: reliability-proportional weights, no zero unless absent
explicit documented weights + scenario set
weights re-derived per fielding

pros.claim: Explicit reliability-proportional weights make the composite's assumptions auditable and testable rather than a hidden default
pros.example: documenting a 0.5/0.3/0.2 revealed/poll/store split lets a reviewer challenge and perturb it

cons.claim: Any weight choice is a judgement that can be wrong, and a confident split can launder bias into apparent rigor
cons.example: an over-weighted poll makes an incentive-inflated category look like the top pick

failure_modes: hiding the weights inside an unstated default
zeroing a signal entirely rather than down-weighting it
acceptance_tests: the weights are stated as reliability-proportional, documented explicitly with a small scenario set, non-zero unless the signal is absent, and re-derived per fielding
revisit_triggers: the reliability grades change
a signal is validated against realized sales
the sensitivity check flags the ranking as weight-fragile

base.update_signal: the reliability grades or a signal validation changes

nodes.definition: Enforce the anti-over-fitting discipline on the owner's existing data: a candidate is never ranked on store history alone, and thin per-candidate store evidence is shrunk toward the broader market prior (Bayesian/empirical-Bayes shrinkage) so a two-order 'bestseller' regresses toward the category mean rather than topping the list [FACT-method: regression to the mean, regularization]. The store signal is capped in influence by its reliability weight and its recency decay, and any candidate whose rank is driven >50% by store data is flagged for review. This is the guardrail that keeps the launch from over-fitting to a small, stale, survivorship-biased past instead of the fuller three-signal read.

included: never rank on store data alone
shrinkage of thin store evidence toward the market prior
flag candidates whose rank is store-data-dominated

pros.claim: Shrinkage toward the market prior stops a tiny-sample store fluke from being crowned a hero
pros.example: a ring with two lucky orders regresses toward its category mean instead of leading the ranked list

cons.claim: Shrinkage can also mute a real owner-specific edge (a niche the store genuinely owns)
cons.example: a legitimately distinctive local-favorite gets pulled toward a generic prior that misses its true pull

failure_modes: ranking a candidate on store history alone
letting a small-sample store bestseller top the list without shrinkage
acceptance_tests: the rule that store data alone never ranks a candidate, shrinkage of thin store evidence toward the market prior, and a flag for store-data-dominated ranks are all stated
revisit_triggers: the store history grows enough to trust less shrinkage
an owner-specific niche is validated as real not fluke
the market prior itself is updated

base.update_signal: the store history size or the market prior changes

nodes.definition: Define and recompute the aggregation that turns the normalized, weighted signals into one composite demand score per candidate. Two interchangeable forms: (a) reliability-weighted mean of the normalized per-signal scores; (b) rank aggregation (Borda / weighted Borda) across the three signal rankings — more robust when a signal is ordinal or has outliers. Both are combined with the OVERFIT_GUARD shrinkage so thin-evidence candidates pull toward the prior. Worked shape: composite = w_market*z_market + w_poll*z_poll + w_store*(shrunk, decayed z_store), renormalized. The rule is stated so the composite reproduces from the inputs, and rank aggregation is preferred whenever the signals are more trustworthy in order than in magnitude.

included: weighted-mean and rank-aggregation forms
shrinkage folded in
a reproducible composite formula

pros.claim: A stated aggregation rule makes the composite reproducible and challengeable rather than a black-box score
pros.example: writing composite = 0.5 z_market + 0.3 z_poll + 0.2 z_store_shrunk lets anyone recompute and audit a candidate's rank

cons.claim: A single scalar composite hides which signal drove a rank, obscuring disagreement
cons.example: two candidates with the same composite can be a market favorite and a poll favorite, a difference the scalar erases

failure_modes: using a weighted mean where signals are trustworthy only in order (rank aggregation was right)
collapsing to a scalar without carrying which signal drove it
acceptance_tests: a reproducible composite (reliability-weighted mean or rank aggregation, with shrinkage folded in) is stated and recomputes from the normalized weighted inputs
revisit_triggers: signals shift from magnitude-trustworthy to order-trustworthy or vice versa
the weighting scheme changes
disagreement between signals becomes frequent

base.update_signal: the aggregation form or the weighting changes

nodes.definition: Attach an honest uncertainty to each candidate's composite score, because a rank without a confidence is a false-precision trap. Confidence rises with signal agreement, total sample behind the candidate and reliability of the contributing signals; it falls with disagreement, thin/absent signals and heavy reliance on the shrunk store estimate. Express it as an interval or a tier (high/med/low) around the composite so downstream reads the ranking as 'A clearly ahead, B and C overlapping' rather than a spurious strict order. Candidates whose intervals overlap are treated as tied, not falsely separated by a decimal of composite score.

included: confidence rising with agreement/sample/reliability, falling with disagreement/thinness
interval or tier around each composite
overlapping intervals treated as ties
excluded: the hard floor to rank at all (MINIMUM_SIGNAL_THRESHOLD)

pros.claim: A confidence interval per candidate prevents a decimal of composite score being read as a real ranking gap
pros.example: flagging B and C as overlapping stops the launch from over-trusting B just because its score is 0.02 higher

cons.claim: Intervals widen the apparent set of contenders, which can feel like indecision to a stakeholder wanting a clean order
cons.example: reporting five candidates as a tied A-band frustrates a request for a strict 1-2-3

failure_modes: publishing a strict rank order that ignores overlapping confidence
letting a shrunk thin-signal candidate carry unwarranted high confidence
acceptance_tests: each composite carries a confidence interval or tier that rises with agreement/sample/reliability and falls with disagreement/thinness, and overlapping intervals are treated as ties
revisit_triggers: a new signal wave tightens or widens a candidate's interval
signals move from agreement to disagreement
sample size behind a candidate changes

base.update_signal: a signal wave changes a candidate's interval

nodes.definition: Provide the decision procedure for when signals disagree — the poll loves a shape the store never sold, or the market read contradicts on-site behaviour. Rules: (1) do not silently average away disagreement; record it as reduced confidence (feeds CONFIDENCE_PER_CANDIDATE). (2) Break ties toward the higher-reliability signal (revealed purchase over stated poll preference) per the grading. (3) Apply an agreement bonus — a candidate that all three signals independently favor is more trustworthy than one carried by a single strong signal — and a disagreement penalty. (4) Escalate a high-stakes disagreement (a would-be hero split between signals) to the next poll wave rather than forcing it into a hero slot on contested evidence.

included: record disagreement as reduced confidence
break ties toward higher-reliability signal
agreement bonus / disagreement penalty / escalate high-stakes splits

pros.claim: Explicit conflict rules stop disagreement from being averaged into a misleadingly confident middle
pros.example: a shape the poll loves but the store never sold is held at low confidence and sent to re-poll, not slotted as a hero

cons.claim: An agreement bonus can over-favor safe consensus candidates and suppress a genuine contrarian winner
cons.example: a novel shape only the trend signal caught gets penalized for lacking corroboration it could not yet have

failure_modes: averaging conflicting signals into a falsely confident composite
always deferring to consensus and killing a real contrarian signal
acceptance_tests: disagreement is recorded as reduced confidence, ties break toward the higher-reliability signal, and an agreement bonus / disagreement penalty / escalation for high-stakes splits are all stated
revisit_triggers: a re-poll resolves a previously escalated split
reliability ordering between signals changes
a contrarian candidate is validated or falsified

base.update_signal: a re-poll or reliability change resolves a disagreement

nodes.definition: Handle the cold-start candidate — a shape/finish the owner has never stocked, so its store-history signal is absent, not zero [FACT-method: cold-start problem]. Rank it from the S1 market + S4 poll signals and shrink it toward its category prior rather than letting a missing history bury a promising novel item at the bottom. This resolves the novelty-vs-proven tension: proven store bestsellers carry revealed evidence but may be stale/saturated, while cold-start novelties carry only forward-looking signal but are where growth and differentiation live. The rule: never auto-penalize absent-history to zero; carry cold-start candidates at their available-signal composite with an explicit lower confidence and a 'test-worthy' flag for the launch or the next poll wave.

included: absent store history treated as missing not zero
rank cold-start from market+poll shrunk to prior
test-worthy flag with lower confidence

pros.claim: Treating absent history as missing not zero keeps promising novel items in contention for the launch
pros.example: a rhodium-plated shape the owner never carried is ranked on market+poll signal instead of being buried at zero

Produce both a global composite ranking and per-stratum rankings (top earrings, top necklaces, top mid-tier, etc.), because kb2 must assemble a balanced set across categories and price-points, and a purely global list could return six variations of one hot category. Stratified ranking also surfaces the best candidate in a thin-signal category that a global list would bury, giving the launch-set builder real options per axis rather than a monoculture.

nodes.definition: Assemble the single ranked candidate list that is the spine of this KB: each candidate row carries its composite demand score, its confidence tier, the driving signal(s), the store-data-dominance flag, and its stratum. Candidates are ordered by composite within confidence-respecting bands (overlapping-confidence candidates shown as a tied group, not falsely separated). The list is explicitly a demand-signal ranking, not a margin or feasibility ranking, and every score is tagged as an [ESTIMATE] synthesized from [METHOD] signals — never a measured demand figure. nodes.definition: Classify the ranked list into A/B/C bands by cumulative demand-signal share using the Pareto/ABC lens [FACT: the ~80/20 principle is a well-established inventory/assortment heuristic, not a measured share for this catalog]. Sort candidates descending by composite, accumulate signal share, and cut A (the vital few carrying the bulk of the signal), B (moderate) and C (the long tail). The band cuts are set by the actual observed cumulative curve, not by forcing a literal 80/20 — the heuristic names the shape, the data sets the cut. A/B/C gives the launch-set builder a principled way to concentrate on the A band while keeping B/C as coverage/optional picks.

included: A/B/C banding by cumulative signal share
Pareto ~80/20 as shape not asserted catalog share
cuts set by the observed curve
excluded: measuring how concentrated the curve is (DEMAND_CONCENTRATION_DIAGNOSTIC)

pros.claim: ABC banding gives a principled concentrate-vs-cover structure instead of an arbitrary top-N cut
pros.example: cutting A at the observed elbow of the cumulative curve focuses the launch on the candidates carrying most signal

cons.claim: Forcing a literal 80/20 when the real curve is flatter or steeper mis-sizes the A band
cons.example: imposing 80/20 on a diffuse category invents a concentration the signal does not show

failure_modes: asserting a literal 80/20 as this catalog's measured share
cutting A/B/C at fixed counts ignoring the observed curve shape
acceptance_tests: the ranked list is banded into A/B/C by cumulative signal share with the ~80/20 Pareto stated as a [FACT] heuristic shape and the cuts set by the observed curve, not asserted as catalog share

the cumulative curve shape changes with new signal
the launch-set builder needs a different A-band size

base.update_signal: the ranked list or its cumulative curve changes

nodes.definition: Measure how top-heavy the demand-signal curve is, because the right assortment shape depends on it: a highly concentrated curve (a few candidates carry most signal) argues for a hero-heavy launch, while a flat/diffuse curve argues for broader coverage. Read the concentration with a ratio (share of signal held by the top-k candidates) or a Gini-style inequality read on the composite distribution [FACT-method]. The diagnostic sizes the A band honestly — it tells the launch-set builder whether to bet on 2-3 heroes plus fillers or to spread across a flatter field — and flags when the curve is so flat that no candidate is a clear hero (a signal-quality warning, not a mandate to invent one).

concentration -> hero-heavy vs broad-coverage implication
flat-curve = no-clear-hero warning

cons.claim: Concentration metrics on a small, noisy candidate set can themselves be unstable
cons.example: a Gini on a handful of shrunk composites can swing on one candidate's re-score

failure_modes: reading a hero into a flat curve that has none
computing concentration on so few candidates that the metric is noise
acceptance_tests: a concentration read (top-k share or Gini-style) is stated with its hero-heavy-vs-broad-coverage implication and a flat-curve no-clear-hero warning
revisit_triggers: the composite distribution changes shape
the candidate set grows or shrinks materially
a hero emerges or dissolves with new signal

base.update_signal: the composite distribution shape changes

nodes.definition: Translate the classification into a hero-SKU vs long-tail structure for the launch: A-band, high-signal, high-confidence candidates are hero-SKU candidates that justify concentrated inventory depth and marketing spend; B/C-band candidates are long-tail options that add category coverage, cross-sell and stacking breadth but individually carry little signal [FACT-concept: long tail]. State the core tradeoff for a six-SKU launch — concentrating on 2-3 heroes maximizes expected sell-through but raises single-bet risk, while spreading across the tail buys coverage and learning at the cost of depth. This node hands kb2 a labelled hero/tail structure, not the final six, so kb2 can balance heroes, coverage and its production constraints.

included: A-band -> hero candidates, B/C -> long-tail coverage
concentrate-vs-spread tradeoff for a six-SKU launch

cons.example: betting the launch on one hero hoop that under-converts leaves no depth elsewhere to carry it

failure_modes: forcing heroes when the concentration diagnostic showed no clear hero
spreading so thin across the tail that no candidate gets launch-worthy depth
acceptance_tests: A-band mapped to hero candidates and B/C to long-tail coverage, with the concentrate-vs-spread tradeoff stated and a labelled hero/tail structure handed to kb2
revisit_triggers: the concentration diagnostic re-reads hero-heavy vs flat
kb2's coverage/depth needs change
a hero candidate is validated or falsified

nodes.definition: Stress-test the ranking against the weight choice, because the weights are the most judgemental input. Re-run the composite under perturbed weight scenarios (revealed-heavy, balanced, poll-informed; poll down-weighted; store data at zero decay vs strong decay) and record which candidate orderings flip. A top set (and especially an A-band) that survives reasonable weight perturbation is trustworthy and can be handed off with confidence; an ordering that flips on a small weight nudge is flagged as a weight artifact and routed back to WEIGHTING_SCHEME or to a re-poll for firmer evidence, not shipped as a finding. The check turns 'we picked weights' from a hidden risk into a stated robustness statement.

included: re-running under perturbed weight scenarios
flagging order-flips as weight artifacts
routing fragile orderings back to weights or a re-poll

pros.claim: A robustness check separates rankings that are real from rankings that are weight artifacts
pros.example: an A-band that holds across revealed-heavy and balanced weights can be handed off confidently

cons.claim: Perturbation testing adds work and can paralyze if every close pair is treated as fatally fragile
cons.example: flagging every adjacent swap as a flip stalls a decision the confidence bands already covered

failure_modes: shipping a ranking whose order flips on a small weight change as if it were firm
over-flagging benign close-pair swaps as fragility
acceptance_tests: the ranking is re-run under perturbed weight scenarios, order-flips are flagged as weight artifacts, and fragile orderings are routed back to WEIGHTING_SCHEME or a re-poll
revisit_triggers: the weighting scheme changes
a new signal shifts the composite
a previously robust ordering becomes fragile

base.update_signal: the weighting or a signal shifts the ordering

nodes.definition: Define the floor of combined, reliability-weighted evidence below which a candidate must not be ranked on noise. When a candidate's total signal (after reliability weighting, decay and shrinkage) is below threshold — e.g. present in only one thin signal with wide confidence — its position would be driven by noise, so it is parked as [UNKNOWN] / needs-more-signal and fed into the next S4 poll wave or a public-data deepening rather than assigned a spurious rank. This is the honest counterpart to CONFIDENCE_PER_CANDIDATE: confidence grades how firm a rank is; the threshold decides whether a candidate earns a rank at all. It prevents the launch from acting on a phantom ordering of near-zero-signal candidates.

included: a signal floor below which a candidate is parked not ranked
route sub-threshold candidates to the next poll/data wave
threshold decides rank-eligibility, confidence grades firmness

pros.claim: A rank-eligibility floor stops the launch from acting on a phantom ordering of near-zero-signal candidates
pros.example: a candidate seen only in one thin poll option is parked for re-polling instead of given a false rank

cons.claim: Too high a threshold parks genuinely promising thin-signal novelties that deserved a trial
cons.example: a strong single-signal cold-start gets shelved when a small test would have been cheap and informative

failure_modes: ranking a near-zero-signal candidate on noise
setting the threshold so high that all novel candidates are parked
acceptance_tests: a minimum signal floor is stated below which a candidate is parked as [UNKNOWN]/needs-more-signal and routed to the next poll or data wave rather than ranked on noise
revisit_triggers: a parked candidate gains signal in a new wave
the cost of a launch trial drops enough to lower the threshold
the signal-quality baseline changes

base.update_signal: a parked candidate gains signal or trial cost drops

nodes.definition: Enforce the honesty contract across the whole ranking: every figure is tagged [FACT] (with basis — e.g. the Pareto/ABC and long-tail concepts, the FTC finish definitions framing the candidate tiers, the regression-to-the-mean / cold-start methods), [ESTIMATE] (a synthesized composite score, with its method and confidence), [METHOD] (a way to obtain a number the signals have not yet measured), or [UNKNOWN] (sub-threshold or absent). No market size, unit-sales count, gold-plated-vs-solid percentage, ethnicity purchase rate, competitor brand or price is asserted as measured anywhere in the ranking; composite scores are explicitly synthesized [ESTIMATE]s over [METHOD] signals, and the actual demand numbers are produced later by the polls and public-data pulls this KB directs.

included: tagging every figure [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN]
no asserted market/demographic/brand/price number
composite scores as synthesized [ESTIMATE]s over [METHOD] signals
excluded: the downstream demand measurement (polls / public-data pulls)

pros.claim: A tag on every figure keeps the ranking trustworthy and prevents a synthesized score being read as a measured demand fact
pros.example: labelling a candidate's 0.7 composite an [ESTIMATE] over [METHOD] signals stops it being quoted as 70% demand

cons.claim: Pervasive tagging adds friction and can be dropped when the list is summarized downstream
cons.example: a screenshot of the top rows can lose the [ESTIMATE] tags and read as measured

failure_modes: a synthesized composite circulating as a measured demand percentage
an invented market share, brand or price slipping in untagged
acceptance_tests: every figure carries a [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] tag, no market/demographic/brand/price number is asserted as measured, and composite scores are labelled synthesized [ESTIMATE]s over [METHOD] signals
revisit_triggers: a downstream summary strips the tags
a real measured demand number arrives to replace an [ESTIMATE]
a new claim type needs a basis tag

base.update_signal: a measured number replaces an estimate or a tag is dropped

nodes.definition: Compose the hand-off to kb2_launch_set_of_six and the downstream assortment work: deliver the ranked candidate list with per-candidate composite [ESTIMATE], confidence tier, driving signal, ABC band, hero/tail label and stratum, plus the robustness statement (which orderings are firm vs weight-fragile), the parked sub-threshold candidates, and the honesty tags. State the boundary explicitly — this KB ranks by demand signal only; kb2 owns balancing category coverage, price-spread, cohesion and pruning against MOQ/plating-run/capital constraints, and jewel_economics owns margin. The hand-off names the conditions kb2 must respect: do not treat a tied group as strictly ordered, re-confirm heroes that were weight-fragile, and re-poll parked candidates before promoting them.

failure_modes: handing off a strict order that drops the tied-group and fragility caveats
letting the demand ranking be treated as the final six without kb2's constraint pruning
acceptance_tests: the hand-off delivers the ranked list with confidence, ABC band, hero/tail label, robustness statement, parked candidates and honesty tags, states the demand-signal-only boundary, and names the conditions kb2 must respect

conflict_axes.name: existing_store_data_vs_overfit_risk
conflict_axes.description: The owner wants the launch built on existing bestseller data ('mindful of the old stuff'), but that data is a small, stale, survivorship-biased sample of only what was already stocked; leaning on it risks over-fitting the launch to the past.
poles: trust the owner's existing store history
shrink and discount it against over-fitting
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use store data as one reliability-weighted, recency-decayed, shrunk-to-prior signal and never rank a candidate on it alone

conflict_axes.name: revealed_purchase_vs_stated_poll
conflict_axes.description: Revealed purchase (marketplace/store) is more trustworthy but broad or thin, while the paid poll is targeted at the 18-25 female buyer but stated, self-selected and incentive-skewed; either can be over-weighted.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: grade both on the five reliability axes and weight revealed purchase above stated preference, but keep the poll non-zero as the only signal targeted at the exact buyer

conflict_axes.name: proven_bestseller_vs_novel_coldstart
conflict_axes.description: Proven store bestsellers carry revealed evidence but may be stale or saturated, while novel cold-start candidates carry only forward-looking market+poll signal but are where differentiation and growth live.
poles: give novel cold-start items a fair shot
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat absent history as missing not zero, rank cold-start on market+poll shrunk to prior, and carry it with lower confidence and a test-worthy flag

conflict_axes.name: hero_concentration_vs_coverage_spread
conflict_axes.description: Concentrating the six on 2-3 A-band heroes maximizes expected sell-through but raises single-bet risk, while spreading across categories/price-bands buys coverage and learning at the cost of depth.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the concentration diagnostic decide — top-heavy curve justifies heroes, flat curve favors coverage — and hand kb2 both structures

conflict_axes.name: single_composite_score_vs_signal_transparency
conflict_axes.description: A single scalar composite is easy to rank on but hides which signal drove a candidate and whether the signals agreed, obscuring disagreement and fragility.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the composite plus its driving signal, confidence tier and disagreement flag so the scalar never hides the underlying agreement structure

conflict_axes.name: global_ranking_vs_stratified_ranking
conflict_axes.description: A single global list ranks by raw signal but can return six variations of one hot category, while stratified ranking preserves coverage but may promote a weak winner in a low-demand stratum.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: produce both and hand kb2 the global order plus per-stratum options so it can enforce coverage without promoting genuinely weak stratum winners

conflict_axes.name: literal_pareto_vs_observed_curve
conflict_axes.description: The ~80/20 Pareto heuristic is a convenient default for cutting the A band, but the actual cumulative signal curve may be flatter or steeper, so forcing 80/20 invents a concentration the data does not show.
poles: cut at the observed curve elbow
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use Pareto as the shape and the concentration diagnostic to set the real cut from the observed curve, never asserting 80/20 as this catalog's measured share

conflict_axes.name: act_on_thin_signal_vs_wait_for_more
conflict_axes.description: A near-zero-signal candidate can be ranked now to keep the list complete, or parked for more polling; ranking it acts on noise while parking it delays a possibly cheap, informative trial.
poles: park sub-threshold candidates for more signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: park candidates below the minimum signal floor as [UNKNOWN]/needs-more-signal and route them to the next poll wave rather than ranking them on noise

conflict_axes.name: firm_ranking_claim_vs_weight_fragility
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want a firm ranking to act on, but the weights are judgemental and an order that flips under small weight changes is a weight artifact, not a finding.
poles: flag and route back weight-fragile orderings
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hand off only the orderings that survive weight perturbation as firm, and mark fragile ones for re-weighting or a re-poll before kb2 acts on them

dominance_rules.rationale: the existing history is a small, stale, survivorship-biased sample that over-fits the launch to the past if it dictates a rank
dominance_rules.trigger: a candidate's rank is driven >50% by store history
dominance_rules.action: shrink the store signal toward the market prior and require market+poll corroboration before the rank stands

dominance_rules.rule: Revealed purchase dominates stated poll preference when they conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: revealed marketplace/store purchase is more trustworthy than a stated, self-selected, incentive-skewed poll vote
dominance_rules.trigger: the poll and a revealed signal disagree on a candidate
dominance_rules.action: break the tie toward the revealed signal while keeping the poll non-zero as the only buyer-targeted signal

dominance_rules.rule: Absent store history is missing, never zero
dominance_rules.rationale: a never-stocked shape has no data, not a measured no-demand result, so zeroing it buries viable novelty
dominance_rules.trigger: a cold-start candidate has no store record
dominance_rules.action: rank it from market+poll shrunk to prior with lower confidence and a test-worthy flag

dominance_rules.rule: Disagreement lowers confidence; it is never averaged away
dominance_rules.rationale: combining conflicting signals into a confident middle hides real uncertainty
dominance_rules.action: apply a disagreement penalty, record reduced confidence, and escalate high-stakes splits to a re-poll

dominance_rules.rule: The observed concentration curve dominates the literal 80/20
dominance_rules.rationale: Pareto names the shape, but the real cumulative curve sets the honest A-band cut
dominance_rules.trigger: an ABC cut is being forced at a literal 80/20
dominance_rules.action: cut A/B/C at the observed curve elbow via the concentration diagnostic and flag a flat curve as no-clear-hero

dominance_rules.rule: Weight-robust orderings dominate weight-fragile ones at hand-off
dominance_rules.rationale: an order that flips under small weight changes is a weight artifact, not a demand finding
dominance_rules.trigger: an ordering flips under weight perturbation
dominance_rules.action: hand off only weight-robust orderings as firm and route fragile ones to re-weighting or a re-poll

dominance_rules.rule: Overlapping-confidence candidates are a tied group, never a strict order
dominance_rules.rationale: a decimal composite gap inside overlapping intervals is not a real ranking gap
dominance_rules.trigger: candidates within overlapping confidence are being strictly ordered
dominance_rules.action: present them as a tied group and forbid strict ordering within it

dominance_rules.rule: A synthesized composite is never a measured demand number
dominance_rules.rationale: the honesty contract forbids asserting market/demographic/brand/price figures the signals have not measured
dominance_rules.trigger: a composite score is about to be quoted as a demand percentage or share
dominance_rules.action: tag it a synthesized [ESTIMATE] over [METHOD] signals and restate the no-measured-number boundary

dominance_rules.rule: Below the minimum signal floor, a candidate is parked not ranked
dominance_rules.rationale: ranking a near-zero-signal candidate gives the launch a phantom ordering to act on
dominance_rules.trigger: a candidate's combined signal is below threshold
dominance_rules.action: park it as [UNKNOWN]/needs-more-signal and route it to the next poll or public-data wave

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the candidate frame and map every signal onto it before combining anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-deriving the whole synthesis after discovering signals were compared at incompatible grains

anti_rework_rules.rule: Characterize each signal's bias and reliability before weighting, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a composite built on an over-weighted biased signal that must be re-run once the bias surfaces

anti_rework_rules.rule: Normalize signals to a common scale before applying weights
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a widest-unit signal silently dominating and the ranking having to be recomputed once noticed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Shrink thin store evidence toward the prior from the first composite
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a small-sample store fluke being crowned a hero and later retracted after the launch is built on it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach confidence and run the weight-robustness check before hand-off
anti_rework_rules.prevents: kb2 building the six on a weight-fragile ordering that flips when the weights are revisited

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat absent store history as missing not zero from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: burying viable cold-start novelties at zero and re-surfacing them only after the launch set is fixed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every figure [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[METHOD]/[UNKNOWN] as it is produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a synthesized composite circulating as a measured demand number and having to be walked back downstream

anti_rework_rules.rule: Park sub-threshold candidates for re-polling rather than ranking them on noise
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a phantom ordering of near-zero-signal candidates driving launch picks that the next wave overturns

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new S4 poll wave or public-data pull lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-ingest the signal, re-grade reliability, and re-run the composite, confidence and ranked list

iteration_protocol.trigger: the store accumulates materially more orders or a never-stocked category is trialled
iteration_protocol.action: reduce shrinkage/decay on the now-thicker store signal and re-rank affected candidates

iteration_protocol.trigger: the weight-robustness check flags an ordering as weight-fragile
iteration_protocol.action: revisit the weighting scheme or switch the aggregation to rank aggregation and re-run the check

iteration_protocol.trigger: a parked sub-threshold candidate gains signal in a new wave
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate it against the minimum floor and rank it if it now clears

iteration_protocol.trigger: the cumulative demand curve changes shape (concentration rises or flattens)
iteration_protocol.action: re-cut the ABC bands and re-map the hero/tail structure for kb2

iteration_protocol.trigger: kb2 requests a re-cut, tighter bands, or different coverage strata
iteration_protocol.action: regenerate the stratified rankings and hand-off structure to kb2's spec

iteration_protocol.trigger: a measured demand number arrives that can replace a synthesized [ESTIMATE]
iteration_protocol.action: swap the estimate for the measured value, re-tag it, and re-run the affected composites

priority_rationale: The candidate frame, signal inventory, store-data intake, reliability grading, recency decay and normalization come first because nothing can be combined until the three heterogeneous signals are mapped onto one frame, characterized for bias, decayed for staleness and put on a common scale; the weighting scheme, overfit guard, combination rule, confidence, conflict resolution, cold-start handling and stratified ranking are the core synthesis that turns those inputs into one reliability-weighted, uncertainty-tagged composite and ranked list; and the ABC/Pareto classification, concentration diagnostic, hero/tail mapping, sensitivity check, minimum-signal floor, honesty ledger and hand-off come last because they read the ranked list to structure it for the launch, stress-test it, keep it honest, and pass it cleanly to kb2 without overstepping into set-building or economics.
